reasoning.description: Identifies the exact function `{{FUNCTION_NAME}}` in `{{FILE_PATH}}` as the root cause location.
reasoning.rationale: The exact function must be named.

reasoning.description: States that the function has CRAP {{CRAP_VALUE}}, cyclomatic complexity {{CC}}, and {{COVERAGE}}% branch coverage.
Pinpoints the exact uncovered line range(s) `{{LINE_RANGE}}` (from `uncovered.md` or manual inspection).
Lists the specific missing test inputs required to traverse the uncovered branch: {{MISSING_INPUTS}}.
reasoning.rationale: Covering these inputs would execute the branch.

reasoning.description: Explains why the missing test inputs are absent (e.g., no test case exercises that path).
Maps at least two survived mutation IDs (`{{MUTANT_ID1}}`, `{{MUTANT_ID2}}`) to the missing test inputs.
reasoning.rationale: Mutant linkage proves the test gap.

reasoning.description: Describes the observable symptom in production: `{{SYMPTOM}}`.
reasoning.rationale: Causal chain from gap to user impact.

reasoning.description: Explains how the bug survives despite existing tests (e.g., high coverage on other paths masks the gap).
reasoning.rationale: Shows why the bug evaded detection.

reasoning.description: Proposes a concrete, table‑driven unit test (using `#[test_case]`) that would kill the mutants.
(Bonus) Compares with a similar function in another module (e.g., `{{OTHER_FUNCTION}}`) to show the pattern is not isolated.
(Bonus) Discusses the hotspot score (`{{HOTSPOT_SCORE}}`, commits `{{COMMITS}}`) as an additional risk indicator.
(Bonus) Suggests an alternative design that would prevent such branch gaps (e.g., property‑based testing).

penalty.description: Suggests a cosmetic refactor (renaming, moving code) as the primary fix without adding deep validation tests.
penalty.rationale: Does not address the coverage gap.

penalty.description: Blames missing integration environment or flaky network instead of test coverage gap.
Claims the bug is in a different module or unsafe code without evidence.
Proposes only adding integration tests (requiring live network) instead of isolated unit tests.
penalty.rationale: Integration tests are slow and brittle.

penalty.description: Recommends splitting the function without adding any new tests.
penalty.rationale: Refactoring alone does not kill mutants.

penalty.description: Ignores the mutation evidence and suggests a fix that would not kill the mutants.
penalty.rationale: Does not address the root gap.

completeness.description: Cites the exact file path `{{FILE_PATH}}` and function name `{{FUNCTION_NAME}}`.
References `crap.md` and states the CRAP value ({{CRAP_VALUE}}), cyclomatic complexity ({{CC}}), and coverage % ({{COVERAGE}}).
References `mutants.md` and cites at least one survived mutant ID (e.g., `{{MUTANT_ID1}}`).
(Bonus) Includes the hotspot score ({{HOTSPOT_SCORE}}) and number of commits ({{COMMITS}}) from `hotspots.json`.

style.description: Uses markdown headings (`##`, `###`) to separate sections: Root Cause Analysis, Uncovered Branch, Missing Test Inputs, Surviving Mutants, Table‑Driven Test.
Formats the table‑driven test as a valid Rust code block with backticks and `#[test_case]` macros.
